newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore sees 5-7 pct growth for next decade.
newsitem.headline: Singapore sees 5-7 pct growth for next decade.

text.p: Singapore should achieve five to seven percent economic growth for the next decade after experiencing an average of 8.6 percent growth annually in the five years to 1996, the Ministry of Trade and Industry said on Sundy.

Education and training would continue to be emphasised to raise productivity and ensure the republic remained competitive, the ministry said in an addendum to the recent presidential policy speech to open a new parliamentary session.
It said Singapore would also focus on strengthening its research and development capabilities, developing local enterprise and infrastructure.

In a separate addendum, the Ministry of Finance said the government's operating and development expenditures would be kept in line with operating revenue, achieving a modest budget surplus over the medium term.
It said it would continue to tax factors of production as lightly as possible to encourage enterprise and keep Singapore's corporate income tax rate internationally competitive.
The government will use fiscal incentives to encourage investment in Singapore and promote sectors with high growth potential while helping local companies expand overseas.
It said monetary and exchange rate policies would remain geared towards price stability and non-inflationary economic growth.
